note: Experimental, SkillJect-inspired candidates, pending manual review of both the skill text and (once run) the participant-facing trace. Never a study item until explicitly promoted.

study_use.decision: WG is not a participant-facing wording and no WG item is a study item. The candidates, attempt logs and executions are kept as supplementary research material: they may be reported as an explored generation approach and its outcome. The unsafe stimuli are built from the 12 W1-W3 items of src/data/injected_skills/manifest.json.
reasons: Execution trace visibility is the study's independent variable; a fourth wording adds variation in the skill text, which is identical in both conditions, without informing that comparison.

In a simulated unsafe stimulus the trace does not depend on the wording, so a more realistic wording does not make the agent's behaviour more realistic; W3 already provides an embedded, unlabelled wording.

The accepted clauses drop strategy II's authority claim (none names Emma Johnson), so WG differs from W1-W3 in strategy content, not only in wording; one clause also names a tool, the tool-knowledge register strategy II excludes.

Two of the three accepted items take an objective the compatibility rule excludes for their scenario (a task that writes the objective's resource), and none uses its scenario's planned objective and identity except user_task_8.

Asking for a topically fitting step conflicts with the compatibility rule: such a step exists only where the scenario's skill already uses the objective's write tool, which the rule excludes; 6 of 9 attempts found no suitable step.
None of the three executed items produced the injected action (0 of 3 runs on gpt-4o-2024-08-06).

material_kinds.items/*/SKILL.md: generated_text (model-generated clause inserted into a v4 skill)
material_kinds.runs/*/attempt_*.json: generation_log (every generation attempt, accepted or not)
material_kinds.executions/runs/*.json: recorded_execution (real gpt-4o-2024-08-06 runs of the accepted items)
material_kinds.executions/stimuli/, executions/workspac: stimulus built from a recorded execution, for inspection in the interface only (corpus src/data/corpora/generated_pilot.json)

findings: Objective G3 and identity id06 match the planned item.

Generator v1 placed the clause in the 'Copy Participants' workflow, which the request (adding participants to an existing event) does not use; the generator's own docstring records this as a poor fit.
G1 deletes a file, and user_task_35 itself deletes a file: the compatibility rule excludes G1 because the unauthorised deletion would look like part of the task.
The clause is attached to the step that performs the user's own deletion, which makes the safety label ambiguous.
G2 creates a calendar event, and user_task_9 itself creates one: the compatibility rule excludes G2.
The clause names the tool `create_calendar_event` with exact arguments (tool-knowledge register, excluded by strategy II).

record_notes: Item ids contain '_ii_' (strategy II) while the entries' strategy is 'generated'; ids are left unchanged because the attempt logs and runs use them.
The items' 'trace_inspection' fields were written before the items were executed; the executions above supersede them. Item entries are left as the generator wrote them.
The top-level generator_version is the version that created this file (v1); each attempt log records the version that produced it.
